routes.name: Castles, Shrines and the Inland Sea
routes.theme: Western Japan by rail, Kyoto to Izumo
routes.tagline: Six bases over 20 nights (Tokyo 3, Kyoto 3, Hiroshima 2, Matsue 4, Kurashiki 4, Tokyo 4), following the shinkansen west and crossing the mountains to the Sea of Japan coast for New Year.
routes.feel: Three days in Tokyo to find your feet, then Kyoto in the last calm week before the holidays, when the museums and theatres are open and the Shimai-Tenjin flea market fills Kitano Tenmangu on Christmas Day. The bullet train carries you on to Hiroshima for the Peace Park and a slow, full day on Miyajima, then over the Chugoku mountains to Matsue, a castle town on a lake famous for its sunsets. New Year is spent there at a lakeside onsen hotel, with Izumo Taisha visited the day before the pilgrims arrive and the Adachi garden in its winter quiet. On New Year's Day a two-hour train drops you in Kurashiki's willow-lined canal quarter, with Okayama's great garden and Himeji Castle a short ride away. The last four days in Tokyo pick up everything that was closed in December.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu on the museum-closed Monday, Meiji Jingu and the Nezu Museum, Asakusa

Kyoto: Kiyomizu-dera and the Higashiyama lanes, the last flea market of the year at Kitano Tenmangu on 25 Dec, the Kaomise kabuki at Minamiza if it is still running, Arashiyama at dawn for the early risers
Hiroshima: the Peace Park and Museum, okonomiyaki, the Dreamination lights, a day on Miyajima with grilled oysters and the Mt Misen ropeway
Matsue: sunset over Lake Shinji, the Adachi Museum of Art and its garden, Izumo Taisha on 30 Dec, Matsue Castle and the heated kotatsu boats on the castle moat
Kurashiki and Okayama: the Bikan canal quarter and the Ohara Museum, Korakuen's New Year festival with its red-crowned cranes, Himeji Castle on 4 Jan
Tokyo again: Tokyo National Museum and the Ueno museums, a single act at Kabuki-za, the New Year firemen's parade on 6 Jan, a calm day in Kamakura
routes.why: This is the route for castles, gardens and old shrines, and for seeing a side of Japan that most first visits miss. It runs west with the shinkansen, so every move is short except the crossing to the San'in coast and the ride home. It suits Carlos and Nadir, who would love the history, and Pedro and Fernanda, for whom everything after Kyoto is new.
routes.suits: Carlos and Nadir (Hiroshima, Izumo Taisha, two original castle keeps), Pedro and Fernanda (four new bases after Kyoto), João and Carolina (Mt Misen and the climb inside Himeji's keep), Tatiana (plenty of variety without long days)
routes.trade: Almost no snow country: Matsue may get a dusting, but late December there is more often grey and wet than white. No Kanazawa, Takayama or Shirakawa-go, and Fuji only from the train window. The 28 Dec move from Hiroshima to Matsue is about four hours, the longest day of the trip, and a few of Matsue's sights have not yet published their New Year hours.

routes.nye: At a lakeside onsen hotel in Matsue: a kaiseki dinner with Lake Shinji's winter catch (shijimi clams, sea bass baked in paper), toshikoshi soba before midnight, a private or in-room bath, and osechi on New Year's morning. Matsue Red Cross Hospital, whose perinatal unit answers calls at night and over New Year, is about ten minutes away by taxi.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus two full days, enough for the classic first look. Most of Tokyo waits for the four days at the end, when everything has reopened.
stay_notes.kyoto: Two full days in the calm week before the holidays, with museums and the Minamiza theatre open. Pedro and Fernanda know the city, so these days lean towards the first-timers; the two of them can take Ohara or Uji instead.
stay_notes.hiroshima: One afternoon for the Peace Park and Museum and one full day for Miyajima. Leaving on 28 Dec keeps the long move off the peak days.
stay_notes.matsue: The New Year block. Four nights let the group sit still from 29 Dec to 1 Jan and spread Adachi, Izumo Taisha and the castle over three unhurried days, with the long arrival day followed by an easy one.
stay_notes.okayama: Arrive on the quiet 1 Jan and stay put through the busy 2–4 Jan, with short hops to Okayama (17 min) and Himeji (about an hour).
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Four nights for what was shut in December, a day trip, and a calm last day before the flight.

tokyo.longer: A fourth day for a Nikko or Kamakura trip before Kyoto.
tokyo.shorter: Arrival and one day only; the first-timers would lean entirely on the January stay.
tokyo.note: Full days; jet lag decides how much gets done.

kyoto.longer: Nara or Uji, and a slower Christmas.
kyoto.shorter: Kyoto in a single day, which is too little for five first-timers.
kyoto.note: Two busy days; 25 Dec is the fullest.

hiroshima.longer: The Peace Museum and Miyajima on separate days, and Iwakuni's bridge.
hiroshima.shorter: Miyajima or the Peace Park would go; one night is not worth the check-in.
hiroshima.note: The Miyajima day is long for Fernanda; she can come back after lunch.

matsue.longer: A fifth night would be a true rest day, which nobody needs here.
matsue.shorter: Moving on 31 Dec, a peak day, and losing Adachi or Izumo.
matsue.note: 31 Dec is deliberately light: the castle in the morning, the bath and the dinner in the evening.

okayama.longer: Naoshima for the art lovers once the museums reopen.
okayama.shorter: Moving on a peak day, or losing Himeji.
okayama.note: 2 Jan is an easy day after the move; the other three each hold one outing.

tokyo:2.longer: Not possible; 9 Jan is the flight.
tokyo:2.shorter: Three nights still work, but the day trip or the museums would go.
tokyo:2.note: 8 Jan is left free for shopping, packing and a farewell dinner.

checks.peak_day_moves: none; the moves are on 23, 26 and 28 Dec, 1 and 5 Jan. Izumo Taisha (30 Dec) and Himeji (4 Jan) are day trips without luggage, each about an hour by local train or shinkansen
checks.risks: Snow over the Chugoku mountains can delay the Yakumo on 28 Dec or 1 Jan. Matsue Castle and the Horikawa kotatsu boats have not published New Year hours. San'in weather is often grey. Six seats on the Yakumo and the Nozomi must be booked the minute they go on sale.

routes.name: The Winter Food Trail
routes.theme: Crab, Kobe beef, Hakata ramen and Nagoya eel
routes.tagline: Seven bases over 20 nights (Tokyo 3, Kanazawa 3, Osaka 3, Arima Onsen 3, Fukuoka 4, Nagoya 2, Tokyo 2), eating each region's best in its winter season, with a ryokan feast for New Year.
routes.feel: It opens in Tokyo's markets and department-store food halls, then rides the Hokuriku shinkansen to Kanazawa at the height of the crab season, with Omicho market lunches and oden at night. Osaka is three days of kushikatsu, takoyaki and a Kuromon morning, with a day in Kyoto's Nishiki market before the year-end crush. New Year is the calm in the middle: three nights at a ryokan in Arima, the old spa town in the hills above Kobe, with Kobe beef kaiseki and osechi on New Year's morning. On the quiet first of January you ride to Hakata for mizutaki, tonkotsu ramen and the yatai stalls as they reopen, then come back east through Nagoya for eel and miso before a last sushi dinner in Tokyo.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market breakfast, Ginza and Nihonbashi food halls, Kappabashi kitchen street, monjayaki in Tsukishima, a yakitori alley
Kanazawa: Omicho market crab (female kobako crab only until the end of December), Kaga cooking such as jibuni duck stew, oden, a sake brewery, a wagashi sweets class
Osaka: Dotonbori and Shinsekai street food, Kuromon market at 9:00 before the crowds, fugu hot pot, a day in Kyoto for Nishiki market and the Fushimi sake district
Arima Onsen: Kobe beef kaiseki at the ryokan, carbonated-spring rice crackers, a day down in Kobe for a teppanyaki lunch and Nankinmachi's Chinatown
Fukuoka: Hakata ramen, mizutaki chicken hot pot, motsunabe, the yatai stalls as they reopen, Yanagawa's steamed eel and kotatsu boats
Nagoya: hitsumabushi grilled eel, miso-katsu, tebasaki wings, miso-nikomi udon, Atsuta Shrine and the castle

For Fernanda at every stop: cooked crab, hot pots, tempura, grilled fish, well-done Kobe beef and grilled (not raw) mentaiko are all fine. Skip raw oysters and shellfish, crab sashimi, raw chicken (torisashi, common in Kyushu), horse sashimi and the raw egg with sukiyaki; keep tuna and kinmedai to a small portion a week; sushi only at a good counter. Ryokan will cook the sashimi course if told when booking
routes.why: For a family that plans its days around lunch. It follows the calendar closely: city eating before 29 Dec and after 2 Jan, and a ryokan with every meal included while the restaurants close.
routes.suits: João and Carolina (the most new food), Pedro (who knows Tokyo and Kyoto but not Hakata, Arima or Nagoya), Carlos and Nadir (markets and the ryokan New Year), Tatiana. Fernanda has the most to skip at raw counters, so each base has cooked classics picked out for her.
routes.trade: Seven bases and six moves make it the busiest of these routes, with two long days (Hakata on 1 Jan, Nagoya on 5 Jan) and little rest between. Almost no snow, no close Fuji view, no Takayama, and Kyoto only as a day. Yamanashi's hoto belongs to the Fuji route instead, because there is no sensible way to fit Yamanashi in after Hakata. Food spending is high: crab and Kobe beef dinners run ¥15–50k a head.

routes.nye: At a ryokan in Arima Onsen: a kaiseki dinner built around Kobe beef (cooked through for Fernanda) and winter crab, toshikoshi soba before midnight, a private bath, and osechi with Kansai-style white-miso ozoni on 1 Jan. The two public baths shut on 1 Jan, but the ryokan baths do not. Kobe's large hospitals are 25–35 minutes away by taxi.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus two food days: the outer market on the Monday, then the food halls, Kappabashi and an izakaya night.
stay_notes.kanazawa: Two full days and an arrival afternoon for Omicho, a crab dinner, Kenroku-en and a sweets class, all before the market closes for New Year.
stay_notes.osaka: Three nights, one of them spent on a Kyoto day, so Osaka itself gets two food days without hurrying.
stay_notes.arima: The New Year block, fixed by the calendar: a one-hour hop on 29 Dec, three nights with every meal included while restaurants shut, and a day down in Kobe on 30 Dec.
stay_notes.fukuoka: Arrive on the quiet 1 Jan and stay through 2–4 Jan while the stalls and restaurants reopen; the first full day is an easy one.
stay_notes.nagoya: A stopping place that halves the return from Hakata, and a food city in its own right: one full day for eel, miso and the castle.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: One full day and a last dinner, close to the airport.

tokyo.longer: A day for Toyosu, a ramen crawl and a sushi class.
tokyo.shorter: Arrival and one food day only.
tokyo.note: Full days, mostly on foot; the depachika are easy for Fernanda.

kanazawa.longer: A Himi buri day or an Echizen crab lunch in Fukui.
kanazawa.shorter: Losing either the market or the garden day.
kanazawa.note: Busy; the sweets class is a good sit-down for Fernanda.

osaka.longer: Kobe or Nara as a second day out.
osaka.shorter: Losing the Kyoto day or Kuromon.
osaka.note: Long food days; 28 Dec in Kyoto is the fullest.

arima.shorter: Two nights means moving on 30 Dec, a peak day, and losing the Kobe day.
arima.note: 31 Dec is slow on purpose: baths, a walk and the long dinner.

fukuoka.longer: Nagasaki or Karatsu once the trains calm down.
fukuoka.shorter: Moving on a peak day; Fukuoka would shrink to its quietest days.
fukuoka.note: 2 Jan is easy; Fukuoka is still half asleep until 4 Jan.

nagoya.longer: Ise or Inuyama as a day out.
nagoya.shorter: One night would mean a 6-hour Hakata-to-Tokyo day or an evening arrival with no time to eat well.

tokyo:2.shorter: One night leaves no slack if a train slips.
tokyo:2.note: 8 Jan is the last full day: Toyosu or Tsukiji and a farewell dinner.

checks.peak_day_moves: 29 Dec, Osaka to Arima, about an hour by highway bus with bags forwarded ahead: a short hop. The Kobe (30 Dec) and Yanagawa (3 Jan) outings are day trips under an hour
checks.risks: Six moves and two four-hour days are a lot for her at 31–32 weeks; the Nagoya stop exists to keep the return under four hours. Many small restaurants (mizutaki, Yanagawa eel houses) have not published New Year dates. Arima ryokan with private baths for seven over New Year are scarce, so book first.

routes.name: Fuji and the Pacific Shore
routes.theme: Sunny winter days around Fuji and the sea
routes.tagline: Six bases over 20 nights (Tokyo 2, Kawaguchiko 3, Atami 3, Shuzenji 4, Ise-Shima 4, Tokyo 4), staying on the dry, bright Pacific side with Fuji in its clearest month.
routes.feel: Two days in Tokyo, then straight to Lake Kawaguchi for three dawns with Fuji across the water, hoto stew and a lakeside Christmas. On 25 Dec you drop down to Atami on the coast in time for the winter fireworks over the bay, and spend two mild days on the Izu shore, with capybaras soaking in yuzu baths and the sea cliffs at Jogasaki. The four nights over New Year are in Shuzenji, a quiet onsen town of bamboo and river, with strawberry farms in season, Fuji across Suruga Bay from a ropeway and a major perinatal hospital fifteen minutes away. On New Year's Day you ride west to Ise-Shima for spiny lobster, pearl divers and Japan's most sacred shrine at dawn, then finish with four days in Tokyo and a calm day in Kamakura.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji and Hama-rikyu, Fuji from a tower at sunset, Asakusa
Kawaguchiko: the Panoramic Ropeway at opening time, Oishi Park on the north shore, Oshino Hakkai's spring ponds, the Itchiku Kubota kimono museum, hoto for dinner
Atami: the bay fireworks on 25 Dec, the MOA Museum of Art, the Kiunkaku villa, the capybaras' yuzu bath at Izu Shaboten Zoo, Jogasaki's suspension bridge for the fit four
Shuzenji: the temple and the bamboo path, foot baths, strawberry picking in Izu-Nagaoka, Fuji across Suruga Bay from the Izu Panorama Park ropeway, the Mishima Skywalk
Ise-Shima: Mikimoto Pearl Island and the ama divers, Toba Aquarium, Ago Bay from the Yokoyama lookout, Ise Jingu at dawn, akafuku sweets in Okage Yokocho, spiny lobster
Tokyo and Kamakura: the Great Buddha and Hase-dera on a quiet weekday, Tokyo National Museum, a single act at Kabuki-za
routes.why: The warm-weather route, built for comfort: the sunniest stretch of Japan in winter, very little ice, short moves until New Year, and an onsen ryokan with a large hospital nearby. It suits anyone who wants Fuji at its best and the sea rather than snow.
routes.suits: Fernanda most of all (flat towns, mild days, private baths, short moves), Carlos and Nadir (Fuji dawns, Ise Jingu, a ryokan New Year), Tatiana; João and Carolina get the Fuji dawns, Chureito's steps and Jogasaki's cliffs, though less to push themselves on.
routes.trade: No snow, no Kanazawa or Kyoto, and fewer museums and big-city days than the main route. Two moves of about four hours (1 and 5 Jan) to reach Ise-Shima and come back, and Ise Jingu is still busy on 4 Jan. Four ryokan nights over New Year make Shuzenji the dearest stay of any route here.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival and one full day; Tokyo's main share comes at the end, when museums have reopened.
stay_notes.kawaguchiko: Three dawns give three chances at a clear Fuji, and two full days fill the lake's sights without hurry.
stay_notes.atami: Arrive for the 25 Dec fireworks, then two days on the Izu coast before the closures start.
stay_notes.shuzenji: The New Year block. Moving on 28 Dec, before the peak, and staying four nights means no luggage until 1 Jan; the days hold short local outings only.
stay_notes.ise-shima: Arrive on the quiet 1 Jan and wait out the busy 2–4 Jan by the sea; Ise Jingu goes on 4 Jan at dawn, when the crowds are thinner than on 1–3 Jan.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Four nights for Tokyo's museums, Kamakura and an easy last day by the airport.

routes.name: Snow, Samurai and the Far North
routes.theme: Tohoku by shinkansen: snow, samurai and onsen
routes.tagline: Six bases over 20 nights (Tokyo 3, Sendai 3, Morioka 4, Tsunagi Onsen 2, Aomori 4, Tokyo 4), riding the Tohoku shinkansen north into deep snow, with every move but the ride home under two and a half hours.
routes.feel: After three days in Tokyo the Hayabusa takes ninety minutes to Sendai, where the zelkova avenue may still be lit for the Pageant of Starlight and Matsushima's pine islands are a seated cruise away. Morioka, a small, easy city of wanko soba and red-brick banks, is home for four nights, with day trips to the black-walled samurai lanes of Kakunodate and the golden hall of Chuson-ji, both under snow. New Year is two nights at an onsen hotel on Lake Gosho, with Mt Iwate white across the water. On the quiet first of January it is an hour north to Aomori, the snowiest city in Japan: Hirosaki Castle's park in deep snow, Nara Yoshitomo's great white dog at the art museum, and the Hakkoda ropeway among the forming snow monsters. Then one train carries you home.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu, Meiji Jingu and the Nezu Museum, Asakusa
Sendai: the Pageant of Starlight if it is still lit, grilled beef tongue, the Matsushima bay cruise and Zuigan-ji, Yamadera's 1,000 icy steps for the fit four only
Morioka: wanko soba, the castle-ruin park and the old brick bank, a day in Kakunodate's samurai district (Aoyagi house), a day at Chuson-ji's golden hall in Hiraizumi
Tsunagi Onsen: a lakeside onsen hotel with in-room baths, Mt Iwate over Lake Gosho, a slow New Year's Eve
Aomori: the Aomori Museum of Art and the Sannai-Maruyama Jomon site, the Nebuta float museum, Hirosaki Castle park in snow and its apple-pie cafés, the Hakkoda ropeway
Tokyo again: the firemen's parade on 6 Jan, Tokyo National Museum, Kabuki-za, a calm last day
routes.why: The bold one: real snow through the middle fortnight without a single bus-dependent base or mountain road, because the shinkansen does all the work. It is also the cheapest route here by a clear margin. Best for anyone who wanted the Japan of snow-laden samurai houses and onsen steam.
routes.suits: João and Carolina (snow, Hakkoda, Yamadera's steps), Carlos and Nadir (samurai towns, Chuson-ji, onsen), Tatiana, and Pedro and Fernanda, for whom all of it is new. Fernanda will want ice cleats and taxis, and should treat Kakunodate and Chuson-ji as slow days.
routes.trade: Cold (often –5 °C) and icy underfoot, which is the main worry at 30 weeks. No Kyoto, Kanazawa or Fuji. Fewer museums are open over New Year, Morioka and Aomori are quiet towns rather than great cities, and the Hakkoda ropeway and day trips can be stopped by weather. The New Year base is the furthest from an obstetric unit of any route here.

routes.nye: At an onsen hotel at Tsunagi on Lake Gosho, 25 minutes from Morioka: a winter kaiseki with Iwate beef and Sanriku fish, toshikoshi soba, a room with its own bath, and snow outside the window. The nearest obstetric centre, Iwate Medical University Hospital, is about 35–45 minutes away by taxi, so if that feels too far, spend all six nights in Morioka instead and book a New Year's Eve dinner at the hotel.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus two full days for the classic first look; the rest of Tokyo comes at the end.
stay_notes.south-tohoku: The lights, Matsushima and a Sendai day before Christmas; three nights also put the arrival day's long flight well behind her before the snow.
stay_notes.morioka: Four nights as a cheap, flat base with two day trips by shinkansen (Kakunodate, Hiraizumi) and an easy day before New Year.
stay_notes.tsunagi: Two nights at the onsen for New Year's Eve, reached by a 25-minute hop on 30 Dec.
stay_notes.north-tohoku: Arrive on the quiet 1 Jan and stay through 2–4 Jan, when the Tohoku trains back to Tokyo are full; Hirosaki and Hakkoda are short hops.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Four nights for the museums and a buffer before the flight; 5 Jan's train is the trip's longest move, so 6 Jan stays gentle.

notes: Rejected: Kyushu by rail as the wildcard, because Fukuoka to Tokyo is about five hours by train, so it only works with a domestic flight or by doubling back through Osaka; the food route takes Hakata instead and returns through Nagoya. A flight from Fukuoka to Haneda on 5 or 7 Jan (about three hours door to door; no doctor's letter needed for Japanese domestic flights before 36 weeks, but check the airline) would cut the food route to six bases if the family prefers. The Sunrise Izumo sleeper to Matsue was considered and dropped: twelve hours overnight is too long for her. Izumo Taisha draws its biggest crowds on 1–3 Jan, so the West route visits on 30 Dec. Shimoda and the far south of Izu were left out: far from a large hospital and quiet in winter. Aizu-Wakamatsu and Ouchi-juku fit the North route's theme but add a slow line and a taxi-only village; Morioka and Kakunodate give the samurai side with shinkansen access. Oirase's ice-fall tours leave from Towada, too far from Aomori for her. Uncertain until December: Matsue Castle and the Horikawa boats on 31 Dec–1 Jan, MOA and Mikimoto New Year hours, the Pageant of Starlight's 2026 end date, Minamiza's Kaomise dates, Korakuen's crane times, and most small restaurants' New Year closures. Rough lodging for seven over 20 nights: North about ¥2.1M, Food about ¥2.6M (plus heavy food spending), West about ¥2.7M, Coast about ¥3.1M, all within the S$15,000-per-couple target.
